reproduction_target: Derivation, fitting and benchmarking of the differentiable loop extrusion model (dLEM) on public chromatin-conformation data: cooltools-based loading/balancing/interpolation/coarsegraining/log-observed-over-expected preprocessing of 4D Nucleome .mcool Hi-C/Micro-C maps for four human cell lines (Table 1); L-BFGS fitting of the contact-decay (distance-decay) model to per-chromosome diagonal averages; Adam-based direct fitting of the left/right extrusion velocity vectors L and R to 2 Mb contact-map patches; sliding-window whole-chromosome fits with coverage/centrality-weighted averaging; patch-level Pearson correlation evaluation; reconstruction of full contact frequencies by combining the power-law and dLEM components; ENCODE bigWig ChIP-seq/DNase-seq/RNA-seq track binning and directional ('painted') CTCF construction; learned convolution kernels relating tracks to L/R; aggregate-peak-analysis validation via bioframe.pair_by_distance and cooltools.api.snipping.pileup; elastic-net (glmnet, R) prediction of L/R from ENCODE tracks; trans-perturbation dLEM fitting on GEO GSE178982 Micro-C (WAPL and CTCF auxin depletion) including the lambda parameter-transfer experiment and CTCF-motif residual analysis; mouse AID-experiment OLS/grid-search kernel linear models; training of the deep dLEM U-Net head on 128x128 10 kb patches (HFF, chr8/chr9 held out, H1 out-of-distribution); and comparison against the pretrained ORCA (2M) and C.Origami models. No wet-lab work is reported; all steps are computational (W = 0).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis list built from the bioRxiv v1 Methods prose. The JATS .source.xml returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch but HTTP 200 to unauthenticated curl with a browser user-agent; the v1.full HTML was also retrieved (200) as a cross-check. The paper has a Code availability statement (https://github.com/chikinalab/dLEM) but NO Data availability statement: data sources are named in prose (4D Nucleome .mcool files, ENCODE bigWigs, GEO GSE178982) and the specific accessions live in Tables 1-6, which are rendered as images in both the JATS XML and the full HTML, so no ENCODE/4DN accession string could be extracted from the retrieved text. The repository landing page and README were read: the repo root carries pixi.lock, Dockerfile_dev, Dockerfile_prod and docker-compose.yml, and the README advertises `pip install dlem-jax`, `pixi install -e`, and `docker run ghcr.io/dborgesr/dlem:latest`. That lockfile-plus-container claim sets capture_claim=env_lock_claimed and makes this a Stage-2 candidate. Two Stage-1 caveats recorded but NOT scored (they require Stage-2 code reading): (i) the repo has no tags/releases and PyPI carries a single version 0.1.0, so nothing pins the code state to the manuscript; (ii) the paper states fitting and deep-model development were done in PyTorch, while the distributed package is named dlem-jax and its README documents a single-region CLI that explicitly 'does not do genome-wide batch fitting', so whether the published package actually contains the manuscript's analysis scripts is unverified at prose level. Version is capped at 1 wherever the pixi lock claim plausibly covers the step's Python stack, and set to 0 for steps whose software is outside that claim (R/glmnet, unnamed bigWig binning tooling, third-party ORCA and C.Origami models). No wet-lab steps (W = 0).

steps.label: Loading and preprocessing of balanced Hi-C/Micro-C contact-map patches with cooltools (no version in prose): matrix balancing, interpolation of missing values, coarsegraining with default parameters, log transform, and observed-over-expected normalisation by subtracting diagonal averages in log space; resolutions h = 10 kb and h = 2 kb; diagonals collected up to 3.75 Mb

Fitting of the contact-decay (distance-decay) model to per-chromosome diagonal averages with L-BFGS, MSE loss between log data and log prediction, 200 epochs, first 7 diagonals omitted, initial parameters a = 0.05, b = 1.1, c = 0.1, d = 0.01

Direct dLEM fit of the velocity vectors L and R to one contact-map patch (PyTorch): uniform-ones initialisation, detachment rate either fitted from contact decay or fixed at 2.5e-6 * h (0.025 at 10 kb, 0.005 at 2 kb), diagonals 50 kb-1.2 Mb with k = 10 (10 kb) and 25-600 with k = 50 (2 kb), 100 epochs of Adam, L/R clamped to [1e-9, 1], parameter set selected by highest correlation rather than lowest MSE

Whole-chromosome dLEM fitting by overlapping sliding windows: patch size 2 Mb (200 x 200 bins at 10 kb), stride 500 kb (50 bins), 4 estimates per position averaged with weights combining patch coverage (fraction of non-NaN main-diagonal values) and positional centrality; chromosomes 3-8 and 10-13, chromosome 9 excluded

Reconstruction of full contact frequencies by combining the power-law distance-decay component (exponent b, main diagonal normalised to 1) with the dLEM extrusion component as c * dLEM + power-law, rescaled by the fitted scaling parameter a (Fig. 2B)

Chromosome-wide patch-level evaluation for the Fig. 2E violin plots: sliding window with 200 kb step (20 bins) and 2 Mb patch (200 bins) over chromosomes 3-8 and 10-13, per-chromosome fitted detachment rate lambda, Pearson correlation between flattened observed-over-expected data and flattened dLEM prediction

ENCODE track processing: download of ChIP-seq, DNase-seq and RNA-seq bigWigs for H1hESC, IMR90 and K562, binning to 10 kb with both mean and max summary statistics, and construction of directional 'painted' CTCF tracks by multiplying binned CTCF ChIP-seq with binned CTCF motif-orientation tracks; per-feature track selection by highest correlation with dLEM parameters. No binning software is named, no motif-scan tool or motif database is named, and the selected accessions live only in the image-only Tables 2-4

Learning of feature-specific convolution kernels relating ENCODE tracks to L and R: sign-preserving correlation loss, non-negativity constraint on kernel weights, fixed kernel width 25 bins, Gaussian initialisation centred at the kernel midpoint with variance 1 plus small random noise, 250 epochs of Adam

Aggregate-peak-analysis validation of the learned kernels: peak calling by z-score threshold 2.5, paired coordinates via bioframe.pair_by_distance() with 500 kb minimum and 1.2 Mb maximum separation, pileups via cooltools.api.snipping.pileup() with 800 kb flanks on the raw contact-frequency scale, post-pileup diagonal normalisation, APA marginals by summation, 'uncoupled APA' as outer product of X/Y marginals and 'kernel prediction' as outer product of the L and R convolved average peaks

Elastic-net linear models predicting L and R from convolved ENCODE tracks using the glmnet package in R (no R or glmnet version given): three feature sets (all / reduced / CTCF-related), inputs and targets scaled, 5-fold cross-validation, mixing parameter alpha = 0.9 with lambda optimised during training, per-fold evaluation by correlation between predicted and observed parameters

Trans-perturbation direct dLEM fits on publicly available Micro-C and ChIP-seq data from Hsieh et al. under GEO accession GSE178982 (Table 5): per-condition and per-chromosome detachment-rate fitting followed by the C3 direct-fit procedure, chromosomes 14-19 for WAPL and 8-19 for CTCF, untreated versus auxin-treated

Fold-change analysis of averaged dLEM parameters between untreated and auxin-treated conditions, including the z-score <= -2 subset of positions with the most pronounced velocity impediments, with per-chromosome lambda averaging

WAPL lambda parameter-transfer experiment: conversion between the distance-decay exponential exponent d and dLEM lambda via lambda = 2*d*<v>, substitution of lambda across conditions ('UT with lambda dWAPL' and 'dWAPL with lambda UT'), evaluation by normalised mean squared error on log-scale contact frequencies over sliding-window patches across chromosomes 14-19 (stated shift '200Mb', apparently a typo for 200 kb)

CTCF-depletion residual analysis: residuals (UT - dCTCF) for L and R per genomic position, positive-strand motifs against L and negative-strand motifs against R, motif scores converted to z-scores and binarised at z >= 2 ('motif present') versus z < 2 ('motif absent'). Motif source, scan tool and score definition are not named

Mouse AID-experiment linear models: per-track maximum summary and best-replicate selection over the ENCODE tracks of Table 6, fast convolution formulated as an OLS problem with L1 penalty alpha and smoothness penalty lambda, grid search over alpha and lambda in [0, 1], kernel lengths 11/25/51/105/125 and a non-negativity flag, chromosome-level train split with holdout chr19/chr11/chr12, selected optimum alpha = 0, lambda = 1, kernel length 51, non-negativity True; models trained on untreated tracks, evaluated by Pearson correlation over all pairwise holdout-chromosome combinations, with a variant down-weighting CTCF-track coefficients by 0.5 and a one-sided Wilcoxon test between models. Software for this OLS/grid-search step is not named

Training of the deep dLEM model (U-Net-like head with attention-pooling tail over CTCF directional motif matches and DNase-seq signal; 7 encoder/decoder stages, dilated convolutions kernel 3, strided depthwise convolutions kernel 2 stride 2, transposed-convolution decoder with skip connections, final 1x1 convolution with 2 output channels and sigmoid): teacher-forcing and recursive supervision with k sampled uniformly in [1, 15], 128 x 128 patches at 10 kb with 64-bin overlap, HFF cell line with chr8 validation and chr9 test, H1 held out entirely, batch size 64 on one NVIDIA A4500 GPU. No optimiser, learning rate, epoch count, loss weighting or RNG seed is given

Benchmark comparison against the pretrained ORCA 2M model (250 x 250 matrices at 8 kb): cropping 45 bins from each end and rescaling with scipy.ndimage.zoom to 128 x 128 at 10 kb, restricted to chromosome 9 (held-out test split for both models) in HFF. ORCA model version, weights source and inference settings are not stated

Benchmark comparison against C.Origami trained on IMR90, predicting chromosome 1 of H1: CTCF ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq inputs processed with 'C.origami's recommended pipeline', 2,097,152 bp windows as 256 x 256 (8192 bp bins), matched patch starts with the first 157 bins extracted (1,286,144 bp) and zoom rescaling to 8000 bp bins. C.Origami version, checkpoint and the accessions of the CTCF/ATAC inputs are not stated

headline.static_readiness: 0/18 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 13 of 18 computational steps sit at the RI ceiling and 5 fall to NI. The paper is unusually strong on parameters (optimiser, epoch counts, patch/stride sizes, thresholds, initial values and hyperparameter grids are given for nearly every fitting step) and on data provenance in principle (4D Nucleome .mcool, ENCODE bigWigs, GEO GSE178982), and it names a live public code repository. What it does not do anywhere in prose is pin a single software version: cooltools, PyTorch, bioframe, scipy, R and glmnet are all cited without version numbers, so version can only reach 1 via the repository's pixi.lock/Docker claim, and only for steps plausibly covered by that Python environment. The 5 NI steps are those outside the lock claim or outside the package: ENCODE track binning (C7) and the mouse OLS/grid-search kernel fit (C15) name no software at all, the elastic-net modelling (C10) runs in R with no R/glmnet version and no R code evidenced in the distributed Python package, and the ORCA (C17) and C.Origami (C18) comparisons pin neither model version nor checkpoint. Two further ceilings apply even to the RI steps: the repository has no tags or releases (PyPI shows a single 0.1.0) so no code state is bound to the manuscript, and no RNG seed is reported for any stochastic step (kernel initialisation noise C8, deep dLEM training C16, cross-validation splits C10), so bitwise reproduction of the reported figures is not attainable from prose alone.
headline.coverage: 18 computational steps assessed from the bioRxiv v1 Methods prose plus the github.com/chikinalab/dLEM landing page and README prose. No wet-lab or physical steps are reported in this paper (W = 0). Tables 1-6, which carry the 4D Nucleome, ENCODE and GEO sample-level accessions, are image-only in both the JATS XML and the full HTML and could not be read as text; data-axis scores therefore rest on the named public repositories plus the one inline accession (GSE178982).

gaps.where: Methods, every named software dependency (cooltools, PyTorch, bioframe, scipy.ndimage, R, glmnet, ORCA, C.Origami)
gaps.missing: Not one software version number appears anywhere in the Methods prose. Tools are cited bibliographically (cooltools [29], PyTorch [30]) or by name only. The only version-shaped statement in the whole artifact set is the README's 'Requires Python 3.11-3.13', which is a range, not a pin.
gaps.how_to_close: State the exact version of each tool used for the reported analyses in Methods, and cite the specific lockfile revision (pixi.lock commit) that the manuscript's results were produced with.

gaps.where: Whole analysis environment - repository-level capture claim versus manuscript
gaps.missing: The repository carries pixi.lock, Dockerfile_dev, Dockerfile_prod, docker-compose.yml and a published container ghcr.io/dborgesr/dlem:latest, but nothing in the paper or README binds any of these to the manuscript's results. The container is referenced by the mutable tag ':latest' with no digest; the lockfile is on a moving main branch. The R/glmnet analysis (C10) is not covered by the Python lock at all, and no renv.lock or R session record is provided.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish a tagged release (or Zenodo DOI) of the repository state used for the paper, cite the container by sha256 digest rather than ':latest', and add an renv.lock (or fold the R modelling into the pixi environment) so the elastic-net step is inside the same closure.

gaps.where: Code availability - github.com/chikinalab/dLEM coverage of the manuscript's analyses
gaps.missing: The statement says 'Source code and analysis scripts are available', but the landing page shows no tags and no releases, PyPI carries a single dlem-jax 0.1.0, and the README documents only a single-region CLI that explicitly 'does not do genome-wide batch fitting, bigWig track output, or predicted-.cool output'. There is also a framework discrepancy: the paper says fitting and deep-model development used PyTorch, while the distributed package is named dlem-jax. Whether the ENCODE track processing, kernel learning, glmnet modelling, perturbation analyses, deep-model training and ORCA/C.Origami comparison scripts are actually in the repository cannot be established from the landing page and README alone (Stage-2 question).
gaps.how_to_close: Cut a versioned release tied to the manuscript, and add a per-figure mapping (script -> figure) in the README so each Methods paragraph resolves to a runnable entry point.

gaps.where: Data provenance - Tables 1-6 (4D Nucleome Hi-C/Micro-C, ENCODE ChIP-seq/DNase-seq/RNA-seq, GEO GSE178982 sample selection, mouse AID tracks)
gaps.missing: The paper has no Data availability statement. All dataset identifiers are confined to Tables 1-6, which are delivered as images in both the JATS XML and the v1.full HTML, so no 4DN file accession, no ENCODE ENCSR/ENCFF identifier and no GSM-level selection could be recovered from the retrieved text. Only GSE178982 appears inline. Genome assembly builds (hg38? mm10?) are never stated, and the CTCF motif database and scan procedure behind the 'painted CTCF' and motif z-score analyses (C7, C14) are unnamed.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a Data availability statement listing 4DN, ENCODE and GEO accessions as machine-readable text (or a supplementary TSV), state the genome assembly build for human and mouse analyses, and name the CTCF motif database, version and scanning tool.

gaps.where: Stochastic steps C8 (kernel initialisation with 'small random noise'), C10 (5-fold cross-validation splits), C15 (grid-search train/holdout assignment), C16 (deep dLEM training: batch shuffling, k sampled uniformly in [1,15], weight initialisation)
gaps.missing: No RNG seed is reported anywhere, and for the deep dLEM the optimiser, learning rate, number of training epochs/steps and early-stopping criterion are also absent. GPU non-determinism (single NVIDIA A4500) is not addressed. The reported correlations and the trained deep model therefore cannot be reproduced numerically even with an identical environment and identical inputs.
gaps.how_to_close: Report and set explicit seeds for numpy/torch/R, publish the training configuration (optimiser, learning rate, schedule, epochs, loss weighting) and either deposit the trained deep dLEM checkpoint or document deterministic-mode settings.

gaps.where: External baseline models consumed by C17 (ORCA 2M) and C18 (C.Origami trained on IMR90)
gaps.missing: Neither baseline is pinned: no repository revision, release version, checkpoint file, or download location is given for ORCA or C.Origami, and C.Origami's input preprocessing is referenced only as 'C.origami's recommended pipeline'. The CTCF ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq tracks fed to C.Origami have no accessions in text. The scipy.ndimage.zoom interpolation order used for both rescalings is unstated.
gaps.how_to_close: Cite the exact ORCA and C.Origami releases and checkpoint files with download URLs or DOIs, list the accessions of the CTCF/ATAC inputs, and record the zoom order and any other resampling settings.
